answer: Latency triangulation: each agent must answer pings from three randomly chosen verifier nodes, say one near a saffron farm in Iran, one on an ocean cable landing and one beside a Venetian lagoon, within tight windows. Round-trip times pin down physical location, so a thousand fake agents on one server share the same latency fingerprint and get merged into one identity. To pass, an attacker must rent real machines in many regions, paying hosting for every Sybil.
